newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end up on lower inflation news.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end up on lower inflation news.

text.p: * Start of foreign buying in select counters seen
The Philippine equities market finished up on Thursday in heavy volume buoyed by news of lower inflation level for November compared to October.
"Its news on inflation and also positioning for next year. With blue chips rising, it seems there's foreign buying," said Ike Wee, assistant vice-president at Lippo Securities.
The main index soared by 32.46 points, or 1.04 percent, to 3,163.33 at close.
The National Statistics Office announced just before the start of trading that annualised inflation level for November was at 4.5 percent, slightly lower than October's 4.7 percent.
Spencer Yap, research head at BPI Capital Corp, said with most buying concentrated in blue chips and B shares, it was evident foreign investors were once again interested in Philippine stocks.
After modest volumes in the past few days, value turnover in today's trade was above average at 3.3 billion pesos.
All sectors rose. Gainers trounced losers 66 to 49 with 72 issues unchanged.
Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities, said heavy profit-taking may ensue once the index reaches the 3,200 to 3,250 level in the next few days.
